page.layout: One printed page; running head at top centre; main text in one column; a margin note block in the left margin (three-line note "Duorum revelatio- nis modo- rum com- paratio." with its lines set beside the first lines of text). No catchword, no page number printed.

main_text.l: to multò clarissimam & plenissimam.
Q. Audiui de vtroque revelationis

l.i: velim inter se vivam vocé & scriptionem
compares, vt ex hac comparatione appareat
vtra maioris sit dignitatis atque autho-

main_text.l: R. Comparationem duorum mo-
dorum inter se faciam. Comparantur
viva vox & scriptura vel in substantia &
in reipsa quæ his modis revelatur, vel
in ipsis revelationis modis. Si compa-
ratio fiat in re, jam vtriusque æqualitas
est, cum res sit eadem vtrobique: Sin
revelationis modos inter se compares,
profectò non poteft negari vivæ voci
locus priorac dignior, cum viva vox &
antiquior tempore fuerit, & organis
prior fit (os enim organon prius ac dig-
nius est manu) & magis accómoda fit
ad captum rudiorum, ac familiarior do-
cendi ratio. Quamquam sunt quoque
in quibus scriptio vivam vocem ante-
cellat: est enim perfectior & accuratior
quidam revelationis modus perfectio-
ribus docendis conveniens, & firmior
veritatis cuftos. Non est negandum in-
terea

marginalia.note: Duorum revelatio- nis modo- rum com- paratio.

page.notes: Marginal note at left is printed beside the first lines of the paragraph. Last word "tercâ" is printed at the foot right and may be a catchword-like line; read as the last line of text. Some marginal marks (dagger-like symbols) appear at the left of "antiquior" and "prior" lines; the printed reference marks are not clearly legible.
